utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. I will speak in French. [No interpretation into English] Good day. I would like to open the session. I would like to greet everybody. I would like to -- should I start from the beginning? Is it all right now? All right. Very well. I would like to welcome all the parties in the courtroom, the representatives of the Defence, of the Prosecution, all those who are in the courtroom and all the staff that assist us in our work. I'm now going to ask the registrar to call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88/2-T, the Prosecutor versus Zdravko Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Registrar. As you have probably noticed already, the Presiding Judge, Judge Christoph Fluegge was unable to attend the hearing today. Pursuant to Rule 15 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, Rule 15 bis, the Trial Chamber is convinced that despite the absence of the Presiding Judge, it can continue with the hearing today. Pursuant to the seniority of the Judges at this International Tribunal, today I have the honour and the difficult task of presiding over today's hearing and I am hoping that everything will go smoothly. If I'm not mistaken -- last week, we finished at the point when the Prosecution was carrying out its examination-in-chief, which was conducted by Mr. Vanderpuye, the witness was Ms. Erin Gallagher. Am I correct, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: Then we may bring in the witness, please. Madam usher, could you please bring the witness in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness. Please be seated. I would like to remind you that the solemn declaration is still in effect and we are here today to continue with the examination-in-chief by the prosecutor. I am now giving the floor to Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, good afternoon to you and Your Honours, good afternoon to everyone, good afternoon to you, Ms. Gallagher. If I could have in e-court, please, 65 ter 2183. We'll need to go to page 4 and then page 5 of that document. Let's go to page 5, please. Yeah, that's where we were. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: As you recall, when we broke last, we were just beginning to look at the various sections of this proposed -- well, rather, this exhibit, which is the identification of certain Bosnian Muslims who were depicted in video footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tolimir, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to welcome all those present. I would like these proceedings to finish as God wills it, not as I. The monitor is not working. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are just waiting to have the transcript ready for Judge Nyambe, so I just ask for your patience. The transcript now is working. Mr. Tolimir, I think you are also all right. Everything is fine. Very well. Mr. Vanderpuye, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We were looking now at the first page of this exhibit, which falls under the heading of Bosnian Muslims identified as missing. Before we get started with this page I just wanted to ask you if you can tell us basically, Ms. Gallagher, of the 31 individuals that are the subject of this identification book, can you tell us how many of these individuals are missing and how many of them are survivors, as you determined them to be most recently?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the 31, there are now four that are deemed missing, and there are six, seven, let me double check, there are seven that are survivors.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And we will look at that a little bit -- in a little bit more detail as we go along but on this page here, which is page 5, I believe, in e-court -- page 6 in e-court, can you just tell us basically what this photograph depicts initially?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. This is a photograph taken from the Petrovic video on July 13th. These are as you see, the men that are walking alongside trucks and buses, and they are being sent to, in this case, to the buses. They've been separated.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in terms of the date, 13 July, with respect to this Petrovic video, were you able to confirm that is the date in fact that this image was taken?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We've confirmed that by many means and one of them being by Zoran Petrovic himself who took the footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I can take it that you had the opportunity to compare this particular still to the video footage itself?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in terms of the identification of these individuals, we see number 1, it's indicated here is a person by the name of Meho Mehmedovic, and beneath that there is an indication that he was identified by his wife and also by his nephew during interviews with the OTP in June of 2000. Now, with respect to those interviews have you had an opportunity to look at these either statements or have you heard a tape, can you tell us what form they were in?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are written statements, I've read the statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in terms of the process of the identification that was done through these statements, can you tell us how that occurred? Was a photograph shown? Were you able to connect the photograph to this particular exhibit and so on?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these photographs were shown to, for example, Meho Mehmedovic's wife and nephew, and they confirmed by this exact photo and sometimes some additional photographs that this was her husband and his uncle.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And was the process in terms of your review of these identifications, the same with respect to Ahmo Mehmedovic and also Sefko Mujic that are indicated as number 2 and 3 respectively on this page?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was the same process.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: With respect to the statements that are indicated, for each of these three individuals, we see that some are identified by OTP interview statements and then we can see here a reference to an identification by Pasaga Mesic during the Rule 61 hearing, 9 July 1996, with respect to the other statements. Now, with respect to the statement -- I should say the testimony, rather, of Pasaga Mesic, did you have an opportunity to review that?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I reviewed his testimony in the Rule 61 hearing as well as read the statements that he based his testimony on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And are the statements as are indicated here, are they all part of an annex in relation to this particular exhibit? Are they all set out in the exhibit at some point?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, there are two indexes that are part of this book. One for the missing, one for the survivors, and it lists all the statements that were relied upon with the -- for the identifications, both in the year 2000 and 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Does it list statements in that part of the exhibit that aren't listed, for example, on this page?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It will list all the statements that were used based on the identification. In this particular example, for example Ahmo Mehmedovic it says identified by Pasaga Mesic, it doesn't list what statements he used to make the identification but they are listed in the index.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I'd like to do is I'd like to go to annex 3 of this book and I think we may find it on page 35. It's page 36. Thank you very much. All right. And here we can see there is a reference to the testimony transcript of Pasaga Mesic, and what I'd like to do is to go to page -- since I was one off before, I would say page 40. And I think right at the top of the page there we can see a specific reference to Ahmo Mehmedovic and beneath that, well, we can see who identified him. Can you tell us a bit about that?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you can see from the testimony, Ahmo Mehmedovic was identified by a neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could go briefly to page -- I think it should be page 39, and if we take a look, I think if we take a look at line 23, down, we can see there was an identification also of Sefko Mujic who was another person that's referenced on page 6 of this exhibit as we've just seen, and can you tell us a little bit about the circumstances of his identification?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And as you can see from the testimony he was also -- Sefko Mujic was also identified by a neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Back on page 40, you can see also - and perhaps I neglected to mention this before - but you can see also an identification of Meho Mehmedovic and that would be at line 8 of that page, do you see that, Ms. Gallagher?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could just go back to page 6, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: With respect to the identifications that were made by Pasaga Mesic, were these based upon photographic identifications in addition to statements that you referred to?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, Pasaga Mesic had shown photographs to neighbours, relatives, et cetera, who identified the people from the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Were you able to first of all examine such photographs and, if so, were you able to connect them to the photographs, for example, that we see here that are the photographs depicted in this book?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. The same footage was used, the same photographs were taken from the same footage that Pasaga Mesic used in 1996. Sometimes the stills are slightly different. They might be further along in the video, slightly different angle, some of them are exactly the same, but, yes, they are basically the same photographs that he used or basically the same ones that you see in the book, but there is an appendix or an annex that indicates the photographs that he used with the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd just like to go over, before we go to the next page, I'd like to just go briefly to page 30, I believe, in e-court. On this page, we see that it's an identification -- well, it indicates that there is an identification table of missing Bosnian Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if we could just go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you briefly tell us what this shows.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an index showing primarily the identified person, you'll see in the fifth column, how they -- who they were identified by, the relation to that person, if they are wife, brother, neighbour; the photograph that was used for the identification, and you see that in the picture ERN as well as the ERN of the statement; and then the -- which photograph that is in the book; and also the photograph that was used, the Rule 61 exhibit number is the photograph that Pasaga Mesic used and referred to in his testimony and the photographs that were used in identifying the men with the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Does this include the statements from the OTP, those from AID, and any other statements that were used in the identification process of these individuals?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it includes all the statements that were used in this book.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is there any particular -- well, are the OTP statements annotated or indicated in red?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And are these the statements that you relied on in order to identify -- or I should say confirm the identities that are indicated in the book itself?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. I looked at all of these statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I'd like to do then is to go to page number -- should be 7 in e-court. All right. Here we have what appears to be similar footage, can you tell us first of all is it similar footage, is it the same or what its source is?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same footage, it's also from July 13, from the Petrovic video, and it's just shortly I think right after the footage you see before, it's -- there is a short -- short amount of footage that shows all the men that are walking alongside heading towards the buses, so this is part of that same footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And here we have two individuals, one and two, respectively Kasim Hafizovic and Senahid Hafizovic, were you able to confirm their identities based upon the statements that are indicated here?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And with respect to these statements, I can see that, for Kasim Hafizovic, there is a reference to three statements, one from his niece, one from his wife, and one from his cousin respectively, and these are all three OTP interview statements from June of 2000. And then there is an indication of an identification by Pasaga Mesic during this Rule 61 hearing in 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could just go into private session for a moment, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Back in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Prosecutor you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You can see from this document, Ms. Gallagher, that this particular individual identifies Kasim Hafizovic, who was otherwise depicted in this book, and what I'd like to ask you is, is there a particular reason why a statement of identity such as this one is not included as part of the -- part of this exhibit, this book, at the front part where the photograph is or where other documents listing the identity of this individual are located?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I -- I'm not really sure what the decision was at the time as to what should be listed with the photographs and what shouldn't be at the time that the book was made. Sometimes it seems fairly evident that they are going with the identification of an immediate family member, such as a wife or a son, or daughter. But otherwise, it would be speculation on my part.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you know what statements Pasaga Mesic relied on or information Pasaga Mesic relied on in 1996 in order to testify about the identity of these individuals?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pasaga Mesic relied upon the statements that were taken by the Tuzla AID in 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Now, with respect to this we can see that this statement is not included in the up-front part, as I would call it, of the book where the other identifications are included with the photograph contained in the exhibit. Are there other such circumstances or other such cases with respect to the missing individuals that are in the book, that you're aware of?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understand your question correctly, the statements that Pasaga Mesic relied upon are in the index, and in the front part of the book it will -- what you will see -- it says the testimony, the Rule 61 hearing testimony of Pasaga Mesic. It doesn't list in the front part of the book which statements he was looking at. It's in the index where you can find the statements that he relied upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So although this isn't apparent when you look at the identification page of this individual Kasim Hafizovic, it would be fair to say that it should be located inside in the index of all the statements of identity?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Why don't we take a look, then, at 65 ter 2183? Oh, yes, I'm reminded I should tender this particular document, so I am tendering it as 65 ter 6788, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will admit it under seal, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1361 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to go just briefly to 65 ter 2183. I think we will have to go to page 30. I think we should go to the next page. And before we blow it up, Mr. President, I think we should not broadcast it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, this should not be broadcast to the public. You may continue, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Witness, I'd just like to draw your attention, if I could, to, if you look in the left-hand column where you see a reference to 10 B, there is a -- there are several references but it's the second one down, you can see that -- does that reference correspond to the statement that we just took a look at?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, that's the same statement we just saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And it is the case that any such statement that is referred to or relied on, I should say, in the testimony of Pasaga Mesic with respect to the identification of individuals in the book, the photo exhibit, would be contained in this index?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Thanks very much. I'd like to move now to page 8 on this exhibit, please. I think we can broadcast this from this point on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, this photograph may be broadcast to the public. Thank you very much, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Prosecutor, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Gallagher in your earlier testimony you indicated you reviewed documents besides statements including certain autopsy reports in order to confirm the identity and status of some of these individuals that were reported missing. Can you tell us a little bit about this particular photograph, the circumstances, and then about the individual?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, this is the footage from the Petrovic video on July 13th. He is -- Mesa Efendic, he is part of the same group of men that you have seen in the other photographs walking alongside the trucks and buses who have been separated out. And in regards to him, I had read these statements and then there was some other documents that I had also looked at pertaining to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Here we can see there it's indicated that he was identified by his wife and by his neighbour as well?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And there was apparently an identification also by Pasaga Mesic which is included in his testimony, part of this exhibit, as well?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Did you have an opportunity to review an autopsy report for this individual?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If I could have 65 ter 6783, please, in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And here we can see -- well, first of all, do you recognise what this is?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is an autopsy report, and I know from the case number it corresponds with Mesa Efendic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If we could just go into private session for a moment, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, let us move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Back in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please continue, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Here we can see that the cause of death that is indicated here was gunshot wounds to the head and pelvic region, the back. Now, I take it you've had an opportunity to review the whole of the autopsy report?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And given your experience and involvement in the investigation to this point, as concerns the men that are depicted in the photograph on the 13th of July, is this consistent with other information that you have reviewed concerning what happened to other men besides this particular one?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, looking at other autopsy reports, listings on the ICMP list statements, interviewing witnesses, it's consistent.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I'd like to show you is page -- should be page 3 of this autopsy report. Here you can see a little bit more detail about the types of injuries to the body of Mr. Efendic. It talks about in particular with the injuries under item number 2, to the head and neck, it talks about a partially crushed part of his head, a fracture, and it indicates gunshot. It talks about a double crush fracture to the right mandible. Have you had an opportunity to look at the drawings and associated documents concerning this autopsy?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And have you -- are they consistent with the injuries that are described here?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we can go to page 2 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You can see here a description -- I should say of the clothing that was found associated with this body, and here we can see under item B it's described as dark, striped pants, following that you can see a striped light colour pajama bottom, after that you can see a light coloured shirt, buttoned at the front, long sleeve; red cardigan, short sleeved; and then black lower cut boots. What I'd like to do, and I don't know if it's possible, maybe somebody can help me, is to juxtapose this report with the photograph that we have in 2183, that's 65 ter 2183, page 8. If we can show that side by side I think it would be most helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will wait to see the photographs of the documents, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we are able to just focus on the individual in the left, the identified one, with the -- if you can just blow him up that would be -- we don't need the name or anything, just the person. All right. That's not bad. Did you compare the description that is indicated in the autopsy report to the video footage of the person that we have here on the right screen, identified as Mesa Efendic?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. And you'll see especially points out is the light coloured or white button up shirt and the dark red maroon sweater vest or short sleeved cardigan on him.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. What I'd like to show you now is 65 ter 51 -- I'm sorry, 5415, and if we could replace the autopsy report and show that picture side by side to the photo identification book that we have there, and maybe we can rotate it so that we can get it a little bit -- if you can flip it the other way around that would be better, that's it. And we can blow up the photograph so we can compare what we have here. Now, can you tell us a little bit about the photograph we have on the left side of the screen? That's 65 ter -- I think I said it was 5415.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it's a photograph from the exhumation site in Kozluk with the same case ID number as you see in the autopsy, and from the photograph you see some -- you see a body with blue, looks like blue dark pants, a light coloured or white long-sleeved shirt, and then a dark red short sleeved top on top of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in terms of the exhumation photo that we have on the left side of the screen I would note that the autopsy report we looked at a moment ago bears the number KK3543B, and this photograph we don't see the designation B. Although we do see KK3543. Do you know the reason for that?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's going to refer to the main body of the 543KK. It's the -- it's the same number, and any additional letters may be -- will be different body parts or locations associated with that body.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President I would like to tender 65 ter 5145 -- 5415, and I'd also like to tender 65 ter 6783.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one moment, Mr. Prosecutor. I can see Mr. Gajic is on his feet. Go ahead, Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to wish a good afternoon to everyone. We have a problem here and that is that none of these documents has been translated so that Mr. Tolimir is not in an opportunity to look at the autopsy reports or what is noted in this book of identifications, since it is in a language he does not understand. As far as this exhibit is concerned that the prosecutor would like to tender, the position of the Defence is that for now it can only be marked for identification but not admitted until we have the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor, you've heard the position of the Defence. I would like to add a question to that: Are you sure that all these documents that you mentioned, specifically 6783, 6788 and 6789, are all on your 65 ter list?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Let's see. 65 ter -- thank you, Mr. President, 6789 is not part of our 65 ter list, Mr. President, although it is specifically listed in the document which is on our 65 ter list and that is the book that I've been going over with the witness. All of these statements are indicated specifically in that document as the witness has established through her testimony, and the document itself has obviously been disclosed to the accused, both the one I'm using and the underlying statement. So I'll answer your question as follows. It's not on the 65 ter list as a particularised item although it is specifically referenced in a document that is on the 65 ter list and forms an integral part of this particular exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Gajic, you've heard what the prosecutor said about the documents which are part of the greater, bigger document, the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, they are in this bigger document, they have been disclosed. Unfortunately, we still didn't receive the translation. But perhaps I would like to deal with a different question here, which might be related to the question of admission of the autopsy reports through this witness. I'm not sure whether it's the practice, whether it's a uniform practice here at the Tribunal, because I would like to read one paragraph from the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic is kindly asked to slow down when he's reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a decision of the Martic Trial Chamber from the 12th of July, 2007. The passage is short, I'm going to read it so that the Prosecution can be aware of the position of the Defence on the matter of these issues. The paragraph states: "On the 4th of May and the 9th of May 2006, Ari Kerkkanen who was previously employed in the OTP as an analyst of criminal intelligence reports or data testified as a Prosecution witness before the Trial Chamber. His written statement was admitted on the 19th of April, 2006, in a redacted version. The Trial Chamber reminds the parties that Ari Kerkkanen was one of the organisers and participants of a number of OTP missions which were entrusted with searching the archives including the state archive of Croatia for the purpose of compiling documents about the Krajina MUP and the MUP of the RSK. "The Trial Chamber notes that Ari Kerkkanen during his testimony and in his written statement about the documents that were collected presented the positions and drew conclusions from information -- from the documents that the -- from the information contained in the document without being an expert in that field and without having any personal knowledge about that information. Pursuant to that, the Trial Chamber did not accord any weight to those positions, conclusions, and analyses of Ari Kerkkanen." I think that I have finished with reading the passage, so I think we are here in a similar situation. Of course, the question of admitting a document and giving it weight as to its probative value and admission of a witness's statement, these are two different things, and I think that at this point in time, it's important both for the Trial Chamber and the OTP to be aware of the position of the Defence in relation to matters that are being presented through this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Gajic, for your intervention. You did say correctly that the practice of the Tribunal on matters such as these is not completely uniform and that is quite correct. On the other hand, Ms. Gallagher is testifying about very technical things and it seems that what she is doing has to do with the conclusions that we have in front of us, and you know very well that it's one thing to admit a document and it's quite something else to give probative value to a certain exhibit or document. In any case, we know at this point in time that these documents have not been translated yet and you suggested that the documents be MFI'd in the meantime. We would like to hear the position of the Prosecution on this matter now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I was just awaiting the translation. There is a couple of things. One is that Mr. Gajic is correct that admissibility and weight are clearly separate issues in the jurisprudence of the Tribunal, and I think that the testimony of this witness clearly establishes that and speaks to that issue. She he has relied upon this information in reaching certain conclusions concerning the confirmation of the identity and status of individuals that are the subject of 65 ter 2183, which is the photo identification book. This is one of the documents that she relied upon which is connected to other evidence before this Tribunal in terms of establishing the identity of the individual that's depicted, in this case, on page 8 of this exhibit. We feel that it is helpful, certainly, to the Trial Chamber to look at this information, in terms of the reliability -- in terms of assessing reliability of the photo identification book. There are many statements which support the identifications that are indicated in the book, as Ms. Gallagher has testified to. We don't intend to tender every statement because I think that would be really overburdensome to the Trial Chamber and I think it's not necessary to establish the reliability of the identifications that the witness is testifying to. On the matter of the translations we do have a pending translation request as concerns the autopsy report that I have offered into evidence and with respect to the statements, these are, as Ms. Gallagher indicated, by and large Tuzla AID statements, they are already in B/C/S, they have already been disclosed in B/C/S to the accused, and I think the ones that I have any way indicated or intended to use do have translations. I think the one that I put up, I can't remember the number just now but I think very clearly came up in B/C/S, it was signed by an individual who was a protected witness. And so that -- those statements have been translated and they are -- they are available to the accused to inspect. With respect to the photo identification book itself, the one that I've been using, he is correct that that is not translated and there is -- there are two reasons for that. One is that I think it's never actually been translated in any other -- in any prior proceeding but that's not an excuse. In this case, it hasn't been translated yet because it is a work in progress and the final version of that book has yet to be tendered or put before the Trial Chamber. As I indicated at the beginning of this examination, I'm using this book to familiarise the Trial Chamber with the book that is being prepared that will be offered into evidence, obviously disclosed to the accused, but is fundamentally the same, less the updated information that Ms. Gallagher has worked on and is testifying about. So that's essentially, for the purposes of these proceedings, to mark the book itself for identification purposes, I think, is the best thing to do. We will offer new one with the translation to supplant that. In terms of the admissibility of the autopsy report, pending the translation request, I think it's best to mark that for identification as well. But in terms of the Tuzla AID statements, those I would submit should be admitted because they do have translations and they have been available to the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Then we all agree that the autopsy report should be translated to make this a fair trial and so that the Defence can use them as far as statements are concerned. I see that Mr. Gajic is on his feet, so please, go ahead, Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think my colleague maybe made an error but I think that the statements given to the documentation, investigation agency are originally in the Serbian and they were translated into English. I'm only saying this in order to have this perfectly clear for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Gajic, do you want to say that you do have the translation of these documents, then?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we don't have a translation of the autopsy reports and we don't have a translation of the identification book. As for the statements that were given to the AID, they were originally given in the language Mr. Tolimir understands, so perhaps this can only be a question of whether they were then translated into English, and from what I know, I think that they were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We need to find a solution for all of these things. We will leave the autopsy reports aside, which need to be translated. We've got the B/C/S statements that were translated into English, and now, Mr. Vanderpuye, you would like to tender document 5415, which is on your 65 ter list. Is that your position or are we talking about some other document?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President. 5415 is the -- no, no it's the photograph, yes, that's right. I would like to tender that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Trial Chamber has decided that the documents will be given identification numbers and then we will decide later what to do with them. Mr. Prosecutor, please, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour 65 ter 06783 will be MFI P1362, and 65 ter 05415 will be MFI P1363.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Please go ahead, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we can go now to, I think, page 9 of 65 ter 2183. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Here we have another identification, this individual's name is Nazif Krdzic, and you can see here he's indicated or designated by the number 1. The book indicates that he was identified by his wife in an OTP interview in June of 2000 as well as by Pasaga Mesic in his testimony during a Rule 61 hearing in July of 1996. Did you have an opportunity -- this is a little bit different, but did you have an opportunity to review this particular statement concerning this identification?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do actually remember this specific statement by his wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you -- tell us what you remember about that statement, and in just a moment I'll get it up for you.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that he and his wife were in Potocari on the 13th, and that they were moving, they were being moved along to the trucks and buses by the soldiers, and he at -- one point the two of them were being split up, the -- they were wanting to separate him away from her, he go to the bus, she go to the trucks, and she was asking, if I remember correctly, asking why or saying that she didn't want to be separated from him and the Serb officer, soldier, saying, basically -- it's in the statement, but saying, "If you don't want the same thing to happen to you as to him, you should go your separate ways." And that was the last time that she saw her husband.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Just a moment. All right. Can I have 65 ter 2424, please, in e-court. All right. I think I have mixed up, perhaps, the exhibit numbers. Maybe we will get back to that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And just bear with me for a moment. Based on what you recall from the statement itself, is that consistent with the circumstances under which this -- under which this person is -- was last seen in the photographs that you looked at?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's consistent that you see her husband with the other men, and alone with all the men and not with other women, their wives, daughters, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I think we may have found it. If we can go to page 3 in the B/C/S and also page 3 in the English. All right. I think we have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In particular, what I'd like to draw your attention to is the third paragraph in English, here you can see there is a recitation of the circumstances under which Srebrenica fell, where this person indicates that they were shelled and that the following day, a Thursday, you can see that in the middle of the paragraph, that would be 13 July, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, July 13th, is a Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you rely on that in terms of establishing the date of the footage in question in addition to the other information you testified about?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was one more confirmation, corroboration, of July 13th date.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what she describes is that they were told to move towards the trucks in columns, is that consistent with the investigation as you know it?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is that consistent with the photograph in which this particular individual, Nazif Krdzic is depicted and identified?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. You see the men walking alongside there -- mainly trucks right there as well as some buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in particular, you recall the part where she says, and you'll see this I think two sentences from where I've just read, where it says: "The soldier told him that that he should come with us but the same thing will happen to your husband as will happen to you," where she says -- I'm sorry, I've mis-read it. It says: "The soldier told him that he should come with him. I asked the soldier if I could come as well, and the soldier said, okay, you can come, you can come with us but the same thing that will happen to your husband will happen with you." Is that -- you recall that part of the statement; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what did you understand that to mean when you read it?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the context of knowing what did happen, I interpreted that to mean that they would be killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, did you consider the fact that this person describes being separated from her husband as consistent with the investigation and important to the reliability of the video footage that you were comparing for identification purposes?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, if we go to, hopefully, the next page, it should be page 4 I think in both documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, just briefly, I would like to ask Mr. Prosecutor to clarify whether the person he mentions here, Behara Krdzic, is a witness who is under number 72 on the list of witnesses?

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor, I would like first of all to be sure whether this document can be broadcast publicly.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It can be broadcast publicly, yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Therefore, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I am informed that she is actually number 72 on our witness list as has been indicated, and I don't believe she is a protected witness. I hope that clarifies things for Mr. Gajic. If we can go to page 7 in the English, we should be able to see the photograph that she is referring to. 24

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to look at this, Ms. Gallagher?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If we can just -- I'd like to offer this into evidence, Mr. President, this document.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which document, Mr. Prosecutor? The photograph or the declaration of this witness?

utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. The declaration of this witness and I believe it actually includes the photograph, so they are all one -- it's all one document which includes both the statement and photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber will consult.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The witness is a 92 bis witness. utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You want to say that this document was already previously admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think it should have been provisionally admitted, yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Provisionally admitted but what do you mean by that? Do you mean marked for identification or in what way was it provisionally admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good question. I am using unfortunately the language of the decision that decided the 92 bis application by the Prosecution which refers specifically to the admission of certain documents associated with that -- associated with the proffered evidence. I'm not sure, maybe it doesn't use the word "provisionally admitted," maybe it just uses the word "admitted" as distinguished from a 92 ter witness, but the gist of what it is is that it's already been decided by the Trial Chamber that it is relevant and probative evidence to the proffered testimony and for that reason is admitted in this case. Whether it's provisionally or qualified in some other sense, I'm not really sure, although my understanding is that it's in the decision dated 7 July 2010, that's the decision that admitted this witness's evidence pursuant to Rule 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence will not oppose any of the decisions of the Trial Chamber. However, as for this witness, we will most probably request from the Trial Chamber, considering the nature of her testimony, which has now been presented to you, that this witness appear in the courtroom for the purpose of cross-examination, because of the seriousness of some of her claims, which have been presented today, and as for the question whether the witness is included in the 92 bis decision, I would propose that I briefly consult with the OTP during the break so that I can check the decision and then it won't be a problem to make any sort of decision that has to do with admitting this particular statement into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Gajic. The Trial Chamber will also hold some consultations.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I did want to point out --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: One minute, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I just wanted to point out that this particular statement was disclosed back in -- on 7 March 2008. It's not new and it was the subject, as I've indicated, of the Prosecution's 92 bis application, so if the Defence has a different position that they -- than what they took in respect of opposing that application, I don't think now is a good time to deal with that issue and it seems to me that it could have been raised maybe even a year ago. There is nothing new in this statement than what was proffered together with the 92 bis application, which the Defence has been aware of as of its filing and aware of the substance of that statement as of its disclosure back in March of 2008, so I don't know that it's a valid objection at this time to raise. Obviously, we will consider the Defence application, I'll consult with Mr. McCloskey about that, but I think to the extent that it raises an issue that Mr. Gajic has identified as a serious important issue concerning the facts of this case, it's something that should have been raised well before today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. Gajic, I would not like to prolong this discussion. Can you just be brief? What do you wish to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a brief response to what the prosecutor has said. The defence opposed admitting this into evidence on the basis of 92 bis rule, and the only thing that I suggested was that the discussion about this issue be postponed until we can see the specific decision because I cannot remember off the top of my head the decision which relates to each of the more than 100 witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in fact, Mr. Gajic is right and if I understood him properly, he wants to consult the Prosecutor's Office during the break. And as I already pointed out, in view of the Trial Chamber, we will have the occasion to admit this statement when the witness appears in the courtroom. On the other hand, we have already done some research and it seems that this document has not been admitted as yet. So we will now mark it for identification and then, if such a need arises, we shall return to this issue later on. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This will be MFI P1364.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Prosecutor, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I just did want to point out that this is a 92 bis witness, and so she won't be coming to testify in court unless the Trial Chamber revisits its 92 bis decision which I've indicated was decided back in July of this year. Now, I appreciate that the Trial Chamber may not have found a reference to the admission of this document just now, and I think I can find it for you, I can see we are two minutes before the break, and I think I can find it for you and have that information available to you as soon as we return.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Prosecutor. It is not necessary for you to look for this document for the sake of the Trial Chamber. I can see that in one minute it will be the moment when we must take the first break. In the meantime, the legal assistants will join the Judges so that we will try to examine the decision which you're referring to, because it's quite long and I cannot read all of it now, and then once we return to the courtroom we will clarify the issues about this exhibit. So as I said, it is now the time for the break. And therefore, we will now take the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can continue with the trial. Mr. Prosecutor, before we continue, I wish to go back, as I already said, to your request to admit into evidence Exhibit 2124 on the 65 ter list. [Interpretation] Page 30, paragraph 46 -- or, rather -- yes, paragraph 46 [as interpreted]. Notwithstanding the fact that the Prosecution remains free to obtain a new declarations pursuant to Rule 92 bis(i)(b) if it sees fit to do so." [Interpretation] So, Mr. Prosecutor, I think the decision is clear. Your request was denied but without prejudice. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And I appreciate your reading that out into the record. I did become aware of it over the break and I did intend to raise that and bring that to your attention. I discussed it also with Mr. Gajic and you're right, the decision is clear. It appears to be that it's based upon a discrepancy between this tendered statement that is referred to in the motion and its attachment, which the Prosecution will endeavour to clear up so that we can resolve the issue once and for all. But I do appreciate it and I do acknowledge that my remarks concerning the decision and the import of the decision as concerns this particular witness were erroneous. I would, however, like to proceed. I think I may be done with this particular document anyway, and I don't know if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a second, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Prosecutor, I just wanted to tell the Registrar quite precisely what the decision was about this Exhibit 2428. And now you may continue, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I think I had left off with that same document and I had just shown the witness the photograph that was appended to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you compare that photograph to the photograph that's in the book identifying this particular individual, Nazif Krdzic?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And having compared the photograph with the one that is in the book, which identifies this individual, are they the same?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to double check what's in the -- if we can take a look at the one in the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I think we were at page 9 in the book, and that's 2183. First take a look at the photograph that's in e-court. All right. Now we are going to go over to I think it's page 9 in 65 ter 2183. All right. Did you have an opportunity to compare these photographs?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that they are the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And just for the record, it appears that the tape counter that's indicated on both of these photographs looks like 00:03:16:05 and looks like a small 0 or symbol after the 5. We are going to have to go two pages beyond this page. All right. There we are. Wait, that's page 12 for the record. Can you tell us what is depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a photograph of Ramo Osmanovic, and he is in Sandici meadow. We've seen this on the Petrovic video on July 13th, in the afternoon, and the video footage, you see him calling out for his son Nermin.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us anything about the individuals that are behind him on the right side of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. You see a man holding a rifle over his shoulders, and the -- these were both -- these were police, both PJP and Special Police that were guarding the men who had surrendered down to Sandici meadow on that day.

utterances.text: You mentioned something about his son, Nermin. Can you tell us about him? What does the investigation reveal concerning him or what do you know about him?

utterances.text: We never see him surrender, come down, in the video footage but from -- well, from his mother's statement, he is missing and then in -- later in the investigation, we have discovered that his remains were found.

utterances.text: I'd like to show you -- well, we can see on this document first that he was identified, that is, Ramo Osmanovic was identified by his wife and identified by a neighbour in their respective statements to the OTP in June of 2000.
